newsitem.title: SWITZERLAND: Zurich announces Scudder buy for $2 billion.
newsitem.headline: Zurich announces Scudder buy for $2 billion.

text.p: Zurich Group, Switzerland's biggest insurance company in terms of premiums, said Friday it was acquiring U.S. asset manager Scudder, Stevens & Clark for about $2 billion.

The transaction will combine Zurich Group's Chicago-based Zurich Kemper Investments Inc. subsidiary, which has some $80 billion in assets under management, with privately held Scudder's $120 billion mutual fund and asset management business.

"The new firm, headquartered in New York City, will be core to Zurich's global investment management, significantly strengthening Zurich's market position in mutual funds and asset management and strategically positioning the Zurich Group to capitalise on the investment management opportunities emerging throughout the world," Zurich Group said in a statement.

The deal, which rounds out the Swiss group's investment management business, is Zurich's second major purchase of an investment company in less than two years and highlights its determination to be a force in investment management in the United States.

Zurich, which completed its acquisition of Kemper in January 1996, said its corporate strategy was to offer "tailored solutions for financial protection and investment management." It has been actively expanding in both asset management and reinsurance.

Analysts said the combination was ideal in that between 70 percent and 80 percent of Kemper's business is in retail mutual funds, while some two-thirds of New York-based Scudder's business is institutional.

The acquisition also provides Zurich's Kemper with Scudder's direct distribution capabilities and clients, along with greater exposure in the faster-growing equity fund and international fund business segments.
More than 80 percent of Kemper's business is in fixed income and money market funds, a segment not growing very quickly, analysts said.

"Strategically this makes sense, of course, but the purchase price is not yet clear and we don't yet know about the underlying profitability of Scudder," said UBS insurance analyst Thomas Kalbermatten.
